title: Black Light FTL Normalized Tidal Degeneracy Boundary Uncertainty Registry

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Quantify uncertainty in the operational near-degeneracy function used by tidal eigenbranch tracking so Gravitational Plane and Slipstream/Shear navigation can distinguish a physically localized loss of branch identity from an astrometrically uncertain transition.

mathematics.activeScaleSensitivity: dS is sign(lambda_i)a_i, sign(lambda_j)a_j, d||T||_F, or 0 depending on the unique active max branch
mathematics.gammaSensitivity: d gamma = sign(g)(a_i-a_j)^T dT/S - |g| dS/S^2 for a smooth active branch and nonzero g
mathematics.operationalBoundary: h_ij=gamma_ij-gamma_min; h=0 is the operational loss/restoration boundary used by the eigenbranch tracker
mathematics.boundaryFraction: f*=f_a-(f_b-f_a) h_a/(h_b-h_a) under a local linear crossing model
mathematics.boundaryUncertaintyBound: sigma_f,upper ~= [(1-w)sigma_gamma,a + w sigma_gamma,b]/|dh/df|; the linear sum is conservative when cross-sample covariance is unavailable

physicalAssumptions: The model is first-order and piecewise differentiable. It is invalid at an exact eigenvalue-gap cusp g=0, at ambiguous max-function ties in S, or when the inherited tensor-covariance linearization is outside its model domain.
The operational gamma boundary is an engineering identity-loss threshold, not a new law of gravity and not a fictional FTL hazard probability.
Cross-sample covariance is not presently carried, so boundary-location uncertainty is reported as a conservative upper-bound construction rather than a statistically exact one-sigma interval.

The normalization scale is itself uncertain and correlated with the numerator because both derive from the same tidal tensor; the implementation propagates them through a single gradient rather than treating them as independent.

familyUse.gravitic-plane: PRIMARY: operational confidence in where a tidal branch becomes non-identifiable before family-specific shear/fork response is evaluated.
familyUse.slipstream-shear: PRIMARY: uncertainty-aware localization of the ordinary-physics topology transition that can feed a separately sourced shear-lane model.
familyUse.metric-envelope: SECONDARY: confidence in principal tidal-axis continuity near strong normalization competition.
familyUse.inertial-torch: STRUCTURAL/NAVIGATION: branch-identity confidence for tidal-load attitude planning.

generatorRules: Consume tensor covariance and tracked eigenbranch sensitivities from the existing uncertainty authority; do not duplicate source propagation or gravity equations.
Compute gamma uncertainty from the full quotient gradient so numerator and normalization-scale correlation are preserved.
If the active max-function scale is tied within the configured tolerance, return NONSMOOTH_SCALE rather than selecting an arbitrary derivative branch.
If |g| is within the configured gap-cusp multiple of sigma_g, return NONSMOOTH_GAP rather than pretending the derivative of |g| is unique.
If inherited branch orientation/tensor uncertainty is outside its linear model, the normalized-boundary result cannot upgrade it to RESOLVED.
Report the actual gamma_min boundary used by the eigenbranch tracker separately from exact lambda_i=lambda_j coalescence.
Do not interpret a narrow gamma-boundary uncertainty envelope as proof that a fictional FTL shear fork exists.
canonSafeguards: This registry does not establish physical realizability of any FTL family.
gamma_min is a versioned navigation/identity engineering control, not a universal constant of nature.
Ordinary tidal geometry and its uncertainty cannot create, prove, or silently zero an exotic family-boundary hazard.
A selected family used for simulation does not establish race, inventor, manufacturer, owner, vessel, or technology ancestry.
A broad boundary envelope means the operational topology transition is poorly localized; it is unresolved knowledge, not automatically high fictional danger.
A max-function tie or exact-gap cusp is a mathematical non-smoothness and must remain explicit rather than being hidden behind a cosmetically finite error bar.
